theory.title: List Variables: Storing Multiple Related Items
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 displays a damage report showing multiple failing systems.

"PROTO-7, scalar variables only hold one value. But we have five damaged systems. We need a list variable—a collection that holds multiple related items."

What is a List Variable?

A list variable stores an ordered collection of items. Think of it as a numbered storage rack:

  • Item 0: First item
  • Item 1: Second item
  • Item 2: Third item
  • ...

In Robot Framework, list variables use the @{list_name} syntax.

Why Use Lists?

Use CaseExample
Related items @{damaged_systems}, @{test_users}
Iteration Loop through each item
Dynamic data API returns array of results
Test data sets Multiple test inputs to try

Creating Lists: The Create List Keyword

*** Test Cases ***
Basic List
    @{fruits}    Create List    Apple    Banana    Cherry
    Log Many     @{fruits}

What happens:

  1. @{fruits} is created with 3 items
  2. Log Many @{fruits} outputs each item on a separate line

Output:

Apple
Banana
Cherry

List Syntax Rules

  • Definition: @{list} Create List item1 item2 ...
  • Reference: Use @{list} to reference all items
  • Index access: Use ${list}[0] to get specific item (we'll cover this next)
  • @ vs $: @{list} expands all items, ${list} treats list as single object

@ vs $ with Lists

*** Test Cases ***
List Expansion
    @{colors}    Create List    Red    Green    Blue
    
    # Using @{colors} - expands to all items
    Log Many    @{colors}
    # Output: Red, Green, Blue (separate lines)
    
    # Using ${colors} - treats list as single value
    Log    ${colors}
    # Output: ['Red', 'Green', 'Blue'] (Python list representation)

Key difference:

  • @{list}: Expands to individual items (like unpacking)
  • ${list}: Treats the whole list as one variable

The Log Many Keyword

Log Many is specifically designed for lists:

*** Test Cases ***
Log Many Demo
    @{systems}    Create List    Power    Navigation    Life Support
    
    # Without label
    Log Many    @{systems}
    
    # With label
    Log Many    Ship Systems:    @{systems}

Output with label:

Ship Systems:
Power
Navigation
Life Support

Empty and Single-Item Lists

*** Test Cases ***
Edge Cases
    # Empty list
    @{empty}     Create List
    Log Many     Empty list:    @{empty}    # Logs just "Empty list:"
    
    # Single item list
    @{single}    Create List    Only One
    Log Many     @{single}                  # Logs "Only One"

Lists in the *** Variables *** Section

You can define lists at the file level:

*** Variables ***
@{SHIP_SYSTEMS}    Navigation    Power    Life Support    Communications
@{TEST_USERS}      alice@example.com    bob@example.com    charlie@example.com

*** Test Cases ***
Use Predefined Lists
    Log Many    Ship systems:    @{SHIP_SYSTEMS}
    Log Many    Test users:      @{TEST_USERS}

Real-World Example: API Testing

*** Test Cases ***
Test Multiple Endpoints
    @{endpoints}    Create List    /users    /posts    /comments    /albums
    
    Log Many    Testing endpoints:    @{endpoints}
    
    # Later you'll loop through these:
    # FOR    ${endpoint}    IN    @{endpoints}
    #     ${response}    GET    ${API_URL}${endpoint}
    #     Should Be Equal    ${response.status}    200
    # END

List Operations (Preview)

Robot Framework's Collections library has many list operations:

  • Append To List: Add items to existing list
  • Get Length: Count items in list
  • Get From List: Retrieve item by index
  • List Should Contain Value: Verify item exists
  • Sort List: Reorder items alphabetically

We'll explore these in later chapters. For now, focus on creating and displaying lists.

Common Mistakes

  • ❌ Using ${list} instead of @{list} when creating lists
  • ❌ Forgetting spaces between items: Create List Item1Item2 (one item!)
  • ❌ Using commas: Create List A, B, C (creates one item "A, B, C")

MENTOR-9: "Create two lists: one with damaged ship systems, another with priority repairs. Use Log Many to display them. Show me you can organize related data."
